title: Tighten axle nuts after wheel work
summary: Refit a wheel and torque its axle nut so the wheel is straight, the brakes work and nothing works loose.
tools: Box wrench to hold the axle
parts: New cotter pin, if your axle uses one

steps.text: With the wheel in place, check that the brake disc sits inside the caliper, or the drum's torque arm is attached.
On a chain bike, set the chain slack and line up the adjuster marks on both sides of the swingarm.
Thread the axle nut on by hand and snug it down while holding the axle head with the box wrench.
Tighten to the axle nut torque on your spec sheet with the torque wrench.
If the axle has a cotter pin hole, tighten slightly further to line it up; never back the nut off. Fit a new cotter pin and bend the legs.
steps.caution: Reusing an old cotter pin can let it snap off and the nut back out.

steps.text: Spin the wheel and pump the brake several times until it bites firmly before you ride.
steps.caution: Pistons pushed back during wheel removal mean the first brake application may do nothing.
